newsitem.title: MALAWI: Israel to assist in Malawi irrigation programme.
newsitem.headline: Israel to assist in Malawi irrigation programme.

text.p: Israel plans to revolutionise Malawi's weather-driven agricultural industry by introducing sprinkler irrigation by mid-1998 amid fears of an impending drought, an Israeli official said on Wednesday.

Director of the Centre for International Agricultural Development Co-operation, Itzhak Abt, told Reuters 56 sites of 12 hectares each -- benefiting up to 20 households -- had already been identified in the country.
"We've come to an understanding that we should be supporting a more ambitious small and medium-size irrigation project," Abt said in a telephone interview.
"We'll have the project on the ground in early or mid-1998."
Most of Malawi's 45,747 square miles (118,484 sq km) of land is covered by water, much by Africa's third largest Lake Malawi. But a lot of water is washed away unutilised.
Over 200,000 hectares of land is available for irrigation, but only 26,000 hectares have been developed, leaving the rest to rain-fed agriculture.
Abt said Israel would offer six fellowships annually to Malawians for on-the-spot service training in irrigation practice, management and teaching trainers.

He could not say how much the project would cost but added that he hoped other donor agencies and international financiers would show interest since sprinkler irrigation required heavy capital investment.
Israel is working with 12 other African countries on similar irrigation projects.
